text:
kelly-peopleops: Heads-up — we've had three reports this morning where interviewers saw two separate scorecards for the same interview in the UI. They ended up submitting feedback twice which is messing with our de-dup analytics.

mark-recruiting: Is it duplication in the scheduler or a client UI bug? Any pattern for how these interviews were created?

kelly-peopleops: All three were created via the new bulk-import + manual edits flow within a 10-min window. Interview IDs: I-7851, I-7852, I-7857. Looks like one scorecard has the canonical template and the other is an empty/placeholder.

devops: Scheduler logs show two assign_scorecard calls for the same interview within seconds: one from bulk-import service and one from the interactive editor. They race and the editor's later update sometimes creates a duplicate entity instead of updating the existing link.

scott-schedulerbot: [scheduler] 2026-07-15T09:10:11Z INFO assign_scorecard interview=I-7851 source=bulk-import template=backend-v2
scott-schedulerbot: [scheduler] 2026-07-15T09:10:14Z INFO assign_scorecard interview=I-7851 source=ui-editor template=null created=placeholder-obj-593

ella-interviewer: I clicked "Assign" because I didn't see a rubric and then the panel owner added one a few seconds later. Ended up with two entries and I accidentally filled the placeholder too. Now my feedback shows twice.

kelly-peopleops: Impact: duplicated feedback, analytics inflation, and a confusing UI. Priority: high for candidate fairness and data integrity. Proposed steps: (1) quick mitigation: a scheduler change that makes assign_scorecard idempotent — if a non-null template exists, ignore null/placeholder updates from UI within a 5s window, (2) backfill: dedupe duplicate score submissions for affected interviews and merge into a single record, tagging audits, (3) longer term: add a causal test in integration suite to simulate parallel assigns.

devops: I can push the idempotency guard as a small change in the scheduler API: reject assign requests where template==null if there already exists a template link AND request_ts - existing_ts < 10s. Will add a feature-flag and deploy to prod. ETA ~25m for deploy + quick smoke.

mark-recruiting: For backfill, can we identify affected interviews by querying for more than one scorecard linked to an interview created in the last 24h and dedupe where one is placeholder? I'll start that query and export a list. Also need messaging to interviewers: please don't click Assign if you see a team is editing the panel.

scott-schedulerbot: [audit] 2026-07-15T09:25:03Z INFO duplicate_scorecards_found count=3 query=multi_scorecard_recent

devops: Deployed idempotency guard to prod behind feature flag `scorecard-idempotency`. Running smoke: simulated parallel assigns — placeholder suppressed.

kelly-peopleops: Great. Please enable the flag for the next 48h and we'll monitor. Mark, any progress on the list?

mark-recruiting: Exported 3 interviews (I-7851,I-7852,I-7857). I'll coordinate with data-eng to run dedupe rules: keep the non-placeholder responses, merge answers where possible, and mark the duplicate as merged with audit note `dedupe-20260715`. Also will notify the affected interviewers with a short message: "We've merged duplicate submissions for interview I-XXXX into a single feedback entry. No action needed."

ella-interviewer: Thanks for handling this. One suggestion: can we add a small "saving" indicator when assign is in-flight, so interviewers don't click Assign again? Saves accidental duplicates.

devops: Good UX idea — I'll add a thin client change request to show a spinner for assign ops and debounce the button for 10s. Putting it in the next sprint if ops agrees.

scott-schedulerbot: [monitor] 2026-07-15T10:00:00Z INFO monitor_run check=duplicate-scorecard-alert threshold=2/hour current=0

kelly-peopleops: Closing loop for now: idempotency guard deployed, backfill queued and audit tags added, monitor in place, and UI debounce planned. Thanks everyone.

mark-recruiting: Thanks team :thumbsup:

ella-interviewer: Appreciate the quick fix :heart:
